title: Longitudinal monitoring of neuromuscular, biomechanical, clinical and psychological function in transtibial amputees and possible implications for individually optimised rehabilitation processes.
summary: The aim of this project is to clarify and explain the physical and cognitive changes and adaptations after an amputation at the lower leg/shank. Current knowledge is based on cross-sectional studies and therefore gives hardly any information on changes in these functions over time. However, this knowledge is essential to develop and implement efficient and effective rehabilitation measures. Therefore, in this study, Patients with an amputation at the lower leg/shank will be tested extensively and regularly over 1-2 years following their amputation surgery. The tests will focus on movements and functions needed to re-aquire an independant management of every-day-life and a good quality of life. These include safe, healthy and independant standing and walking, mobility and strength for activities of daily living, as well as psychological health. The testing methods herefore include measurement of muscleactivity and strength/force during these tasks, the biomechanics of gait and balance, brain activity to innervate the muscular system and potentially the prosthesis, as well as questionnaires on psychological health. These outcomes will be compared across the different time points as well as to a matched group of non-amputees as healthy controls.
conditions: Acquired absence of leg at or below knee

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- unilateral or bilateral transtibial amputees
- sufficient kognitive function to understand patient information, informed consent and testing instructions
Exclusion criteria:
- additional amputations
- severe neurological diseases or handicaps that may influence the study outcomes
- depression, anxiety or similar psychological diseases for which patients are in treatment
